A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same reconstruction method. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated reconstruction and pose-estimation results, real-robot experiments, and sensing and tactile-noise ablations in Tables 1–3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds component and robustness ablations, DexYCB evaluation, timing results, and a seed-sensitivity example.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same SDF representation, Structure-VAE, multimodal flow model, physical losses, inference guidance, and refinement pipeline. The additional SDF-generation and SAM3D-integration descriptions disclose details without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on DexYCB human-hand scenes, extending the earlier simulated robotic-hand and real-humanoid coverage to an unseen human-hand population with lower-resolution crops and noisy masks. It also introduces controlled mask and kinematic corruption scenarios; existing training datasets and robotic evaluations remain.

E2.justification: The Amodal3R and SAM3D comparisons are retained. New Appendix Table A1 compares against EasyHOI and FollowMyHold on DexYCB, substantially extending comparison to human-hand interaction methods. Appendix B.3 also introduces TRELLIS as a runtime comparator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces the DexYCB evaluation with CD in cm², F5mm, F10mm, I.V., and reconstruction rate, plus component-removal controls and mask perturbations of 2/5 pixels and calibration errors of 5 mm/1 cm. Appendix YCB totals change from 865 grasps/20,760 images to 945/22,680, matching the existing main-text count; this does not establish a rerun. DexYCB quality metrics use differing successful-reconstruction subsets across methods.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds mask and kinematic robustness tests and ablations of inference guidance, training physics losses, and binary versus distance contact channels. Figure A4 adds seed sensitivity for a failure case. Earlier sensing and tactile-noise aggregates are retained, but their occlusion-bin breakdowns are removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies qualitative seed 42, states that quantitative results average different seeds, and identifies seeds 34, 53, and 38 for the illustrated case. No run count or variability estimates are supplied, and the disclosure does not establish increased repetitions.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the retained sensing/noise aggregates are numerically unchanged. New results include CD 0.052 without training physics losses versus 0.033 for the full model, and DexYCB reconstruction rates of 0.99, 0.58, and 0.30 for Ours, FollowMyHold, and EasyHOI. Runtime and seed-dependent outcomes are added; earlier binwise ablation entries are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical representation, objectives, and inference updates in Equations 1–17 are unchanged. Appendix image-processing equations are retained with new numbering. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about metric-scale reconstruction, pose estimation, physical conditioning, and transfer to an unseen robot hand. The added experiments support these retained claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations distinguishing the importance of training physics losses from the smaller contribution of inference guidance, attributing most tactile gains to distance features, and linking real-world degradation to kinematic sensitivity. It adds seed-dependent failure discussion and replaces the broad cross-hand generalization caveat with a limitation concerning camera-aligned coordinates and dynamic multiview fusion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project repository link, SDF-generation details involving winding-number signs and near-surface mesh queries, A6000/H200 stage timings, and explicit SAM3D integration instructions. These are useful additions to implementation and access documentation, without establishing changes to the underlying method.

R1.justification: Related work expands to additional hand-object reconstruction and robotic tracking literature, including FollowMyHold, EasyHOI, AlignSDF, Object Pop-Up, and What's in Your Hands?. This broadens positioning within the retained generative-model and robotics framing. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and author-name corrections, rewrites Section 4.4, reorganizes Appendix A/B, and adds a supplementary title and acknowledgements. Most of the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and conclusion remain closely matched.

P2.justification: A consolidated main-text Table 4 replaces the earlier appendix ablation displays, retaining aggregates and adding grouped experiment rows. v2 adds a DexYCB table and seed-comparison figure, relocates Table 3, and renumbers existing supplementary figures. Existing illustrations are retained, with local resizing, caption edits, and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v1 reported modality benefits without isolating the central physics losses, inference guidance, or contact representation. v2's Table 4 substantially strengthens validation by testing those components and the calibration sensitivity invoked to explain real-world failures. DexYCB broadens transfer evidence, while implementation and seed disclosures improve transparency. Although binwise ablation detail is lost and DexYCB quality comparisons are limited by unequal successful-sample subsets, the new evidence resolves important gaps in support for the unchanged method.
